walkthroughs.body_html: The 'May 16 Notification' (1966) and the August plenum's 'Decision Concerning the Great Proletarian Cultural Revolution' began the upheaval. Mao swam the Yangtze (16 July 1966) to demonstrate vigour. Red Guards rallied at Tiananmen from 18 August 1966. Liu Shaoqi was denounced as China's Khrushchev and died of medical neglect in 1969; Deng Xiaoping was purged.

Factional fighting (the Wuhan Incident, July 1967) prompted PLA intervention. From late 1968 the Down to the Countryside Movement dispersed Red Guards. The Ninth Party Congress (April 1969) named Lin Biao as Mao's successor. The Lin Biao Affair ended on 13 September 1971 with his death over Mongolia, discrediting the cult.

Nixon's visit (February 1972) and Sino-American rapprochement signalled pragmatism. Zhou Enlai promoted the Four Modernisations; Deng was rehabilitated, then purged again after Zhou's death (January 1976). The Tangshan earthquake (28 July 1976) killed at least 240,000. Mao died on 9 September 1976; the Gang of Four was arrested on 6 October 1976 by Hua Guofeng and the PLA.

mcqs.q: Why did the Communists win the Chinese Civil War?
options: Mao's appeal to peasants through land reform, the discrediting of the KMT by corruption and inflation, and the disciplined organisation of the PLA — not foreign aid.
William of Orange was Charles II's son and inherited the throne.
Mao won because the USSR sent the Red Army to help.
Mao won because the USA refused to support the KMT.
